_note: A BATCH. Pure data — no code, no logic, nothing executable. Written by whoever transcribes a sheet of photographs; validated and loaded by batch.js. The procedure is brain-config/hooks/binder-sheet-intake.md. Any key starting with _ is a note to a human and is ignored by the loader.
label: Sheet 3 · Drinks
source: Two photographs from Michael, 2026-07-30. One face each.
_faces_note: WHICH FACE IS THE FRONT IS AN ASSUMPTION unless a photo shows something that settles it. Nothing in these two images does. Beer was called the back on 07-30 and Michael corrected it to the front on 07-31. Keep this honest: 'assumed' makes the preview screen say 'front and back assumed' out loud, right where someone is about to press the button.

sheet.title: Drinks
sheet._id_note: NON-POSITIONAL ON PURPOSE. The older `mini-binder-s1` is the SECOND sheet, because its id was minted from a 0-based order and then everything moved. An id should say what a thing IS, not where it sat the day it was made. sheet_order is deliberately absent — the worker computes MAX+1 at run time, so this lands after whatever exists at the moment it runs.

defaults._note: Applied to every print. Stated once, because the seventeenth copy is where the typo lives.
defaults._retail_note: SOURCED, not assumed. inciardiprints.com/pages/mini-print-vending-machine-1 states the Mini Print Vending Machine prices each mini print at one dollar. DOLLARS, never cents. This is the ARTWORK's retail; what Michael paid is copy.acquired_price and is left empty because nobody knows it.
defaults._edition_type_note: 'open' even for the three Brooklyn Brewery pieces. The brewery called them a limited edition design, but in this schema 'limited' means A RUN OF N NUMBERED IMPRESSIONS. Vending machine minis are not numbered. Marketing language is not an edition type.
defaults._confidence_note: 'named' is honest here ONLY because Ana hand-writes the title on the lower margin of every card, so these were read, not guessed. If a title is inferred from the artwork alone, that print needs its own "confidence": "inferred" — see the per-print override in the hook.
defaults._acquired_where_note: NOT SET, deliberately. Vending machine, pop-up, shop and trade are all plausible and none is known. A plausible guess in a data field is worse than a blank: the blank is honest, the guess is indistinguishable from a fact.
defaults._collection_note: There is no collection_id anywhere in this file and that is CORRECT. artwork.collection_id is a real FK, there is no POST /collection route, and more importantly schema.sql draws the line: a collection is WHAT THE ARTIST RELEASED, a sheet is HOW MICHAEL LAID IT OUT. These eighteen are an arrangement. The SHEET carries the grouping.

_prints_note: side is 'A' or 'B' — what the DATABASE stores (CHECK side IN ('A','B')). Front and Back are what a person reads; binder.js owns that mapping and nothing else should. position is 0-8 in reading order, left to right then top to bottom. The UI shows position + 1.
